title: Duels: A guide to throwing down the gauntlet
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history and rules of dueling, starting with a read-through of a HowStuffWorks article by Ed Grabowski. They cover the etymology of "duel," the role of seconds, the Irish Code Duello of 1777 and its rules on apologies, the no-shooting-in-the-air rule, and how the winner was expected to act. They discuss women duelists such as Lola Montez, the 1804 duel between Alexander Hamilton and Aaron Burr, and dueling as a tool of honor among nobles, a form of trial by combat, and a way to eliminate political rivals. The episode traces the link between dueling and jousting, fencing, and the shift to pistols in America, and it explains why dueling declined after the Civil War and World War I. The episode closes with listener mail and announcements for South by Southwest events and the Amazon Institute contest.

entities.name: Midshipman's Handbook of the U.S. Navy

segments.title: Opening banter and article read
segments.summary: The hosts open by reading Ed Grabowski's article intro on how duels work, with banter about the piece and about the movie The Quick and the Dead.

segments.title: Definition of a duel and the role of seconds
segments.summary: The hosts define a duel as a one-on-one battle, trace the Latin etymology of duello, and describe the role of seconds, who were supposed to keep the peace but often fought as well.

segments.title: Dueling codes and the goal of restoring honor
segments.summary: The hosts describe the dueling codes, including the Irish Code of 1777, and say its rules aimed to injure rather than kill. They explain that duels restored honor after insults and describe the rules for the winner.

segments.title: Women duelists and the Navy handbook
segments.summary: The hosts note the Code Duello was reprinted in the Midshipman's Handbook until 1862 and discuss women duelists, including Lola Montez, along with a tangent about sexism in fights.

segments.title: Apology rules in the Code Duello
segments.summary: The hosts read rules on apologies: the first offender must apologize first, and blows are prohibited among gentlemen, with the alternatives being a cane or exchanging shots.

segments.title: Dueling etiquette and the Hamilton-Burr duel
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how duels were often not fought wholeheartedly, and the rule against firing in the air. They describe the 1804 duel between Alexander Hamilton and Aaron Burr in Weehawken, New Jersey, where Hamilton was shot and Burr was later charged with murder.

segments.title: Seconds, pistols, dueling at night, and duel endings
segments.summary: The hosts describe rules for seconds loading guns in each other's presence, the rule against dueling at night, and the rules for when a duel ends, such as when a party is disabled or bloodied.

segments.title: Dueling among nobility, trial by combat, and jousting
segments.summary: The hosts explain dueling as a privilege of nobles tied to honor and inheritance, how it served to differentiate ranks and resolve debts and land disputes, its use in trial by combat, and its roots in jousting and the chivalric code.

segments.title: Pistols, fencing, and the decline of dueling
segments.summary: The hosts explain how firearms ended the armored joust and led to the sport of fencing, how pistols democratized dueling in America, and why it declined after the Civil War and World War I.

segments.title: Listener mail, announcements, and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts announce South by Southwest live podcast events, promote the Amazon Institute contest, and invite NGOs to request plugs and listener contact.
